email.body1:
Justin, saw Bolt made Affirm the default BNPL across the merchant network and shipped Bolt ID late last year.

Expanding the network like that usually puts more enterprise accounts in play than the team can cover before the next push. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Bolt off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Justin, quick follow-up for Bolt.

As the merchant network grows, enterprise pipeline targets tend to climb faster than headcount, and most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to hit the new number. The gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your enterprise team needs this quarter, plus where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Justin, last bit of proof for Bolt.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Bolt's enterprise reply rate likely compares to other fintech companies. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Justin, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling enterprise pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Rolling out new network features keeps the whole GTM team busy for a while.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to an enterprise motion? I'll tailor it to Bolt either way.
